title: Cancer Cases Surge Among WTC Health Program Patients 25 Years After 9/11
detail: Physicians and patients gathered at Northwell Health's Long Island Jewish Medical Center to mark the approaching 25th anniversary and warn of an accelerating health crisis among the roughly 145,000 people now enrolled in the WTC Health Program. At Northwell alone, annual cancer diagnoses grew from 177 in 2023 to 235 in 2025 — a 75% jump — with 132 new cases already recorded in the first half of 2026, part of 811 new cases logged over the past 42 months versus 1,634 across the entire first decade (2013–2022). Lung cancer cases have doubled in five years. Across the full WTC Health Program population, more than 57,000 cancer cases have now been documented. Dr. Jacqueline Moline, the program's director, said: 'There has been a twofold increase in lung cancer in just five years. Our fear is that cancer diagnoses will only rise as we move into the next 25 years.' The average WTC Health Program patient is now 63 years old; the most common cancers are prostate, skin, breast, and urinary tract.

media.caption: Northwell Health physicians Dr. John D'Angelo, Dr. Jacqueline Moline, and Dr. Craig Devoe discuss the rise in 9/11-related cancers with survivors Felicia Ivey-Toure and Frank Kotnik.

title: 9/11 Responders Face September 11 Deadline to Preserve Workers' Compensation Rights
detail: With the 25th anniversary approaching, attorneys reminded 9/11 rescue, recovery, and cleanup workers that September 11, 2026 is the deadline to file Form WTC-12 with the New York State Workers' Compensation Board. The form is a registration, not a claim itself, but it permanently preserves the right to later file a workers' compensation claim for a 9/11-related illness — critical because cancers and other conditions tied to Ground Zero toxic dust exposure can take decades to appear. It covers anyone who took part in rescue, recovery, or cleanup operations between September 11, 2001 and September 12, 2002 at the World Trade Center site, the Fresh Kills landfill, NYC morgues and temporary morgue facilities, or barges transporting debris — including firefighters, police, sanitation workers, electricians, cleaners, food-service workers, and volunteers. The filing deadline has been extended multiple times since 2006; missing it closes the door on a future claim permanently under current law.

media.caption: 9/11 responders and cleanup workers have until September 11, 2026 to file Form WTC-12 to preserve their workers' compensation rights.
